materials: household-safe materials chosen and approved by the supervising adult

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “why shared spaces need care.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Model one practical routine step by step, name the trusted adult's role and which steps require supervision, practice it safely, finish the whole loop, and transfer the routine to a new setting. Keep the explanation centered on why shared spaces need care. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or tasks about why shared spaces need care. After each step, ask: “What tells you that step is right?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of why shared spaces need care and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about why shared spaces need care; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsafe step, or a weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of why shared spaces need care and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about why shared spaces need care; then identify one check that would catch an error, an unsafe step, or a weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, the safety steps followed, the evidence of a finished loop, and the revision. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for why shared spaces need care, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain, draw, or demonstrate why the process for why shared spaces need care works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of why shared spaces need care, and avoid unnecessary remediation.

accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. A home, a body, a routine, or a family is never described as good, bad, clean enough, or messy.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Guardian permission is required before any real-world task begins, and the guardian chooses which tasks are appropriate for this learner and this home.
A real-world task counts as complete only when a parent or guardian confirms it. A learner self-report alone can record activity but cannot certify an adult-supervised task.
No identifiable learner photo is required. Accept a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, or guardian confirmation instead.
No dieting, calorie targets, weigh-ins, body-size scoring, earned-food framing, or food-morality language is taught, modeled, or requested.
Reflection may be kept private. No learner is required to disclose family circumstances, income, health details, faith, or personal history.
Stop and ask a trusted adult about broken glass, fire, raw-food risk, electrical hazards, heavy objects, leaks, medication, or unknown substances.
A trusted adult must be present for heat, sharp tools, appliances, cleaning chemicals, medication, or transportation, and the adult decides which steps the learner performs.

media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or an adult demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For a real-world household task, record only the guardian permission and the guardian confirmation that the task was supervised and finished.

For a real-world household task, completion evidence also requires a parent or guardian confirmation recorded through the household-authorized adult surface; a learner self-report alone does not certify an adult-supervised task.
extension: Apply reflecting and setting a next step in a different room, at a different time of day, or with a different family member, or teach the routine to someone else with an original example. Do not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. A home, a body, a routine, or a family is never described as good, bad, clean enough, or messy.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Guardian permission is required before any real-world task begins, and the guardian chooses which tasks are appropriate for this learner and this home.
A real-world task counts as complete only when a parent or guardian confirms it. A learner self-report alone can record activity but cannot certify an adult-supervised task.
No identifiable learner photo is required. Accept a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, or guardian confirmation instead.
No dieting, calorie targets, weigh-ins, body-size scoring, earned-food framing, or food-morality language is taught, modeled, or requested.
Reflection may be kept private. No learner is required to disclose family circumstances, income, health details, faith, or personal history.
Stop and ask a trusted adult about broken glass, fire, raw-food risk, electrical hazards, heavy objects, leaks, medication, or unknown substances.
A trusted adult must be present for heat, sharp tools, appliances, cleaning chemicals, medication, or transportation, and the adult decides which steps the learner performs.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, labeled photograph of a finished routine, worked checklist, or adult demonstration supporting reflecting and setting a next step.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or an adult demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For a real-world household task, record only the guardian permission and the guardian confirmation that the task was supervised and finished.
home_connection: With guardian permission, invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of reflecting and setting a next step at home under the supervision the guardian chooses. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
